s1.syndrome_frame: Acute cardiac syndrome with respiratory distress and hemodynamic instability
salient_findings: Severe left ventricular dysfunction on echocardiography
key_facts: Patient in their 20s without noteworthy medical history
Presented with chest pain and dyspnea
Experienced palpitations and symptoms of upper respiratory tract infection 3 days prior
Vital signs: temperature 36.5°C, heart rate 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate 22 breaths per minute, blood pressure 105/70 mm Hg, oxygen saturation 89% on room air
Lost consciousness 20 minutes after arrival with decreased blood pressure
Troponin T elevated at 4.74 μg/L
Pro-brain natriuretic peptide elevated at 4850 pg/mL
C-reactive protein elevated at 18.50 mg/L
Procalcitonin elevated at 39.68 ng/mL
Severe left ventricular dysfunction on transthoracic echocardiography with ejection fraction 38%
Wall motion abnormalities in multiple vascular territories on echocardiography
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography

ECG findings: upward QRS complex in lead aVR, pure R wave in leads V1 and V2, sinus tachycardia, low QRS voltage in limb leads, ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, aVF, and V1-V6, ST-segment depression in leads aVR and aVL

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin T, severe left ventricular dysfunction, and wall motion abnormalities on echocardiography

shortlist.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with chest pain, dyspnea, and hemodynamic instability, with normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin T and ST-segment elevation on ECG, although coronary angiography showed normal coronary arteries

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with chest pain, dyspnea, and hemodynamic instability, with severe left ventricular dysfunction on echocardiography

shortlist.label: Giant cell myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin T, severe left ventricular dysfunction, and wall motion abnormalities on echocardiography, with a potential for rapid progression

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of upper respiratory tract infection 3 days prior, elevated troponin T, pro-brain natriuretic peptide, C-reactive protein, and procalcitonin, along with severe left ventricular dysfunction and wall motion abnormalities on echocardiography, are consistent with myocarditis. The normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography also support this diagnosis, as myocarditis is not typically associated with coronary artery disease.

rejected.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While stress cardiomyopathy could explain the left ventricular dysfunction, it does not fully account for the patient's preceding upper respiratory tract infection symptoms or the elevated inflammatory markers.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: The normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography make acute myocardial infarction less likely, as this condition is typically associated with coronary artery occlusion.

rejected.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy is characterized by a specific pattern of left ventricular dysfunction that mimics myocardial infarction but is not supported by the patient's overall clinical presentation and laboratory findings.

rejected.label: Giant cell myocarditis
rejected.why: Giant cell myocarditis is a rare and more severe form of myocarditis, but the patient's presentation and laboratory findings are more consistent with a viral or inflammatory etiology rather than an autoimmune process.
